paragraphs.title: The purpose of the signs and telling the story to future generations

easy.question: Whom did the Lord command Moses to visit?
answers: Pharaoh
Aaron
The Israelites
easy.explanation: The Lord told Moses, “Go in unto Pharaoh.”

easy.question: Whose heart did the Lord harden?
answers: Moses’ heart
Pharaoh’s heart and the hearts of his servants
The Israelites’ hearts
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart and the hearts of his servants.

easy.question: To whom was Moses to tell what happened in Egypt?
answers: Only Pharaoh
Only Pharaoh’s servants
His son and his grandson
easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Moses to tell it “in the ears of thy son, and of thy son’s son.”

medium.question: Why did the Lord harden Pharaoh’s heart and the hearts of his servants?
answers: To display His signs and power among them
To prevent Moses from speaking to them
To keep the Israelites in Egypt
medium.explanation: The passage says this was so the Lord could show His signs among the Egyptians.

medium.question: What does the phrase “what things I have wrought in Egypt” emphasize?
answers: That nothing happened in Egypt
That the Lord had acted powerfully in Egypt
That Moses built cities in Egypt
medium.explanation: The context of the signs and plagues shows that the Lord had acted powerfully in Egypt.

medium.question: What is the connection between telling future generations about the signs and knowing that the Lord is God?
answers: The story preserves only people’s names
The story hides the Lord’s actions
The story helps future generations know the Lord
medium.explanation: The passage connects telling the story to future generations with knowing that the Lord is God.

challenge.question: What can we conclude from the Lord mentioning both the son and the grandson?
answers: The message of the Exodus should pass from generation to generation
Only the first generation needed to know about the signs
The sons were supposed to remain in Egypt
challenge.explanation: Mentioning the son and grandson shows that the memory and meaning of the Lord’s acts were to be passed on to later generations.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “in the ears of thy son” indicate about how the story should be told?
answers: It should be written secretly
It should be told directly and clearly to children
Children must not hear it
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates direct spoken communication so that the children can hear and understand the story.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the phrase “my signs which I have done among them”?
answers: The signs would happen only in the future
The signs were an imaginary story
The signs had already been performed among the Egyptians
challenge.explanation: The words refer to signs the Lord had already performed in Egypt and among its people.

questions.question: What can we conclude from the Lord mentioning both the son and the grandson?
answers: The message of the Exodus should pass from generation to generation
Only the first generation needed to know about the signs
The sons were supposed to remain in Egypt
questions.explanation: Mentioning the son and grandson shows that the memory and meaning of the Lord’s acts were to be passed on to later generations.

questions.question: What does the phrase “in the ears of thy son” indicate about how the story should be told?
answers: It should be written secretly
It should be told directly and clearly to children
Children must not hear it
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates direct spoken communication so that the children can hear and understand the story.

questions.question: What can we understand from the phrase “my signs which I have done among them”?
answers: The signs would happen only in the future
The signs were an imaginary story
The signs had already been performed among the Egyptians
questions.explanation: The words refer to signs the Lord had already performed in Egypt and among its people.

paragraphs.title: Warning of the plague of locusts

easy.question: Who came to Pharaoh and spoke to him?
answers: Moses and Aaron
Moses and Joshua
Aaron and Miriam
easy.explanation: The passage says that Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh.

easy.question: What did Moses and Aaron demand of Pharaoh?
answers: That he build new houses
That he let the Israelites go
That he give them food
easy.explanation: They told Pharaoh, “Let my people go, that they may serve me.”

easy.question: What plague was about to come if Pharaoh refused?
answers: Locusts
Darkness
Blood
easy.explanation: Moses warned, “To morrow will I bring the locusts.”

medium.question: What would happen if Pharaoh refused to let the Israelites go?
answers: The locusts would reach only the wilderness
The locusts would cover Egypt and eat the vegetation
The Egyptians would immediately leave their homes
medium.explanation: The locusts would cover the land and eat what remained after the hail, including the trees.

medium.question: What does the phrase “the residue of that which is escaped” refer to?
answers: What remained after the hail
Only the food inside the houses
All the plants that remained untouched
medium.explanation: It refers to the vegetation that survived the hail.

medium.question: Why are Pharaoh’s houses, his servants’ houses, and all the Egyptians’ houses mentioned?
answers: To show that the locusts would affect every part of Egypt
To announce that only Pharaoh’s servants would survive
To describe Moses’ travels through Egypt
medium.explanation: The passage emphasizes that the locusts would fill every household throughout Egypt.

challenge.question: What can we conclude from the word “to morrow”?
answers: The plague would come at an unknown distant time
The plague was expected the very next day
The plague had already ended
challenge.explanation: “To morrow” means that the locusts would come on the following day.

challenge.question: What does the description that the locusts would cover “the face of the earth” show?
answers: There would be only a few locusts
The locusts would appear in one house
There would be so many locusts that the ground could not be seen
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes such a vast swarm that the land would be hidden from view.

challenge.question: What is unusual about the plague described in verse 6?
answers: No previous generation in Egypt had seen anything like it
It would affect only the Israelites
It would occur only after the Exodus
challenge.explanation: The passage stresses that this would be an unprecedented event in Egypt for many generations.

questions.question: What can we conclude from the word “to morrow”?
answers: The plague would come at an unknown distant time
The plague was expected the very next day
The plague had already ended
questions.explanation: “To morrow” means that the locusts would come on the following day.

questions.question: What does the description that the locusts would cover “the face of the earth” show?
answers: There would be only a few locusts
The locusts would appear in one house
There would be so many locusts that the ground could not be seen
questions.explanation: The phrase describes such a vast swarm that the land would be hidden from view.

questions.question: What is unusual about the plague described in verse 6?
answers: No previous generation in Egypt had seen anything like it
It would affect only the Israelites
It would occur only after the Exodus
questions.explanation: The passage stresses that this would be an unprecedented event in Egypt for many generations.

paragraphs.title: Pharaoh’s servants demand that Israel be released

easy.question: What did Pharaoh’s servants ask him to do?
answers: Let the Israelites go and serve the Lord
Punish Moses and Aaron
Stop the feast in Egypt
easy.explanation: Pharaoh’s servants told him to let the people go and serve the Lord.

easy.question: Who asked Moses and Aaron, “Who are they that shall go?”
answers: Pharaoh’s servants
Pharaoh
The Israelites
easy.explanation: Pharaoh asked Moses and Aaron who would be leaving.

easy.question: Whom did Moses want to take to serve the Lord?
answers: Only the elders
Only the men
The entire family, along with the flocks and herds
easy.explanation: Moses said that the young, old, sons, daughters, flocks, and herds would all go.

medium.question: Why did Pharaoh’s servants ask him to let Israel go?
answers: They wanted to leave with them
They realized that Egypt was being destroyed
They were afraid only of Moses
medium.explanation: They said, “Knowest thou not yet that Egypt is destroyed?” because the plagues were causing great damage.

medium.question: In the phrase “your little ones,” whom does Pharaoh mean?
answers: The Israelites’ children
Their servants
Their animals
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the children who might leave with the adults.

medium.question: What was the difference between Pharaoh’s proposal and Moses’ request?
answers: Pharaoh offered to send the flocks, but Moses refused
Pharaoh offered to send only the men, while Moses asked for everyone and their possessions to go
Pharaoh offered to keep them in Egypt, while Moses asked only for freedom to worship
medium.explanation: Pharaoh limited the departure to the men, while Moses insisted that the entire family and livestock leave.

challenge.question: Why did Moses include the flocks and herds in his request?
answers: Because they were Egyptian property
Because he wanted to feed them to the Egyptians
Because the feast to the Lord required the whole group and the animals needed for worship
challenge.explanation: Moses said, “We must hold a feast unto the Lord,” so the livestock needed for worship had to go with them.

challenge.question: What can we understand from Pharaoh’s words, “Evil is before you”?
answers: He tried to frighten them and prevent the families from leaving
He blessed them for their journey
He immediately agreed to Moses’ entire request
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh portrayed their departure as dangerous in an attempt to keep the families from going.

challenge.question: What does Pharaoh’s rejection and expulsion of Moses reveal about his position?
answers: He became convinced that everyone should leave
He agreed to let only the men go and rejected Moses’ request
He asked Moses to stay and celebrate in Egypt
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh limited the departure to the men and then drove Moses and Aaron from his presence.

questions.question: Why did Moses include the flocks and herds in his request?
answers: Because they were Egyptian property
Because he wanted to feed them to the Egyptians
Because the feast to the Lord required the whole group and the animals needed for worship
questions.explanation: Moses said, “We must hold a feast unto the Lord,” so the livestock needed for worship had to go with them.

questions.question: What can we understand from Pharaoh’s words, “Evil is before you”?
answers: He tried to frighten them and prevent the families from leaving
He blessed them for their journey
He immediately agreed to Moses’ entire request
questions.explanation: Pharaoh portrayed their departure as dangerous in an attempt to keep the families from going.

questions.question: What does Pharaoh’s rejection and expulsion of Moses reveal about his position?
answers: He became convinced that everyone should leave
He agreed to let only the men go and rejected Moses’ request
He asked Moses to stay and celebrate in Egypt
questions.explanation: Pharaoh limited the departure to the men and then drove Moses and Aaron from his presence.

paragraphs.title: The plague of locusts covers Egypt

easy.question: What creature came upon the land of Egypt?
answers: Locusts
Frogs
Fish
easy.explanation: The passage says that locusts came upon all the land of Egypt.

easy.question: Who stretched out his rod over the land of Egypt?
answers: Pharaoh
Moses
Aaron
easy.explanation: The passage says, “And Moses stretched forth his rod.”

easy.question: What carried the locusts into Egypt?
answers: Rain
The Nile
An east wind
easy.explanation: An east wind brought the locusts into Egypt.

medium.question: What caused the locusts to arrive in Egypt?
answers: An east wind that blew all day and all night
Rain that fell in the morning
Hail that continued to fall
medium.explanation: The east wind blew all day and night, and in the morning it brought the locusts.

medium.question: In the phrase “rested in all the coasts of Egypt,” what happened to the locusts?
answers: They disappeared
They settled throughout Egypt
They multiplied
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the locusts arriving throughout Egypt and settling there.

medium.question: Why was the land darkened?
answers: Because the sun went down
Because hail covered the sky
Because the locusts covered the face of the land
medium.explanation: The locusts were so numerous that they covered the land and darkened it.

challenge.question: What does the statement “before them there were no such locusts as they, neither after them shall be such” emphasize?
answers: The plague of locusts was unprecedented
The locusts appeared only once a day
The locusts were smaller than usual
challenge.explanation: The statement emphasizes that no swarm before or after would compare with this one.

challenge.question: What did the locusts eat according to the passage?
answers: Only the plants left by the hail
Every herb and all the fruit left by the hail
Only the fruit trees
challenge.explanation: The passage says they ate every herb and all the fruit that the hail had left.

challenge.question: What can we conclude from the fact that no green thing remained in Egypt?
answers: The locusts came before the hail
The locusts ate only the trees
The locusts completed the destruction begun by the hail
challenge.explanation: The hail had left some vegetation, and the locusts consumed what remained.

questions.question: What does the statement “before them there were no such locusts as they, neither after them shall be such” emphasize?
answers: The plague of locusts was unprecedented
The locusts appeared only once a day
The locusts were smaller than usual
questions.explanation: The statement emphasizes that no swarm before or after would compare with this one.

questions.question: What did the locusts eat according to the passage?
answers: Only the plants left by the hail
Every herb and all the fruit left by the hail
Only the fruit trees
questions.explanation: The passage says they ate every herb and all the fruit that the hail had left.

questions.question: What can we conclude from the fact that no green thing remained in Egypt?
answers: The locusts came before the hail
The locusts ate only the trees
The locusts completed the destruction begun by the hail
questions.explanation: The hail had left some vegetation, and the locusts consumed what remained.

paragraphs.title: Pharaoh’s regret and the removal of the locusts

easy.question: Whom did Pharaoh call?
answers: Moses and Aaron
The Israelites
Egypt’s officials
easy.explanation: Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron.

easy.question: What did Pharaoh ask Moses and Aaron to remove from him?
answers: The famine
This death
The darkness of night
easy.explanation: Pharaoh asked them to take away “this death.”

easy.question: Where did the wind carry the locusts?
answers: Into the wilderness
To Goshen
Into the Red Sea
easy.explanation: The wind carried the locusts and cast them into the Red Sea.

medium.question: What did Moses do after leaving Pharaoh?
answers: He prayed to the Lord
He gathered the locusts
He sent the Israelites away
medium.explanation: After leaving Pharaoh, Moses entreated the Lord, meaning he prayed.

medium.question: In the phrase “intreat the Lord your God,” what did Pharaoh ask Moses and Aaron to do?
answers: Flee
Pray and plead
Gather the locusts
medium.explanation: Pharaoh asked them to appeal to the Lord in prayer.

medium.question: Why did Pharaoh not let the Israelites go after the locusts were removed?
answers: Moses did not pray
The locusts remained in Egypt
The Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart
medium.explanation: The passage explicitly says that the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that the locusts completely disappeared from Egypt?
answers: Not one locust remained anywhere in Egypt
Pharaoh called for Moses
Moses left Pharaoh
challenge.explanation: The statement that not one locust remained shows that the swarm disappeared completely.

challenge.question: What was the difference between Pharaoh’s words and his actions?
answers: He asked for help but did not confess his sin
He confessed his sin but ultimately did not let Israel go
He let Israel go but then changed his mind
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh said, “I have sinned,” and asked for prayer, but he still refused to release Israel after the plague ended.

challenge.question: What can we understand from Pharaoh’s request to remove “this death”?
answers: He wanted to punish Israel
He thought the locusts were harmless
He wanted immediate relief from the danger and suffering
challenge.explanation: His request shows that he wanted the present danger and suffering removed at once.

questions.question: Which detail emphasizes that the locusts completely disappeared from Egypt?
answers: Not one locust remained anywhere in Egypt
Pharaoh called for Moses
Moses left Pharaoh
questions.explanation: The statement that not one locust remained shows that the swarm disappeared completely.

questions.question: What was the difference between Pharaoh’s words and his actions?
answers: He asked for help but did not confess his sin
He confessed his sin but ultimately did not let Israel go
He let Israel go but then changed his mind
questions.explanation: Pharaoh said, “I have sinned,” and asked for prayer, but he still refused to release Israel after the plague ended.

questions.question: What can we understand from Pharaoh’s request to remove “this death”?
answers: He wanted to punish Israel
He thought the locusts were harmless
He wanted immediate relief from the danger and suffering
questions.explanation: His request shows that he wanted the present danger and suffering removed at once.

easy.question: What did the Lord command Moses to stretch out?
answers: His hand toward heaven
His rod over the Nile
His hand over the land
easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Moses to stretch out his hand toward heaven.

easy.question: How long did the darkness last in Egypt?
answers: One day
Three days
Seven days
easy.explanation: The passage says that the darkness lasted three days.

easy.question: What did the Israelites have in their dwellings?
answers: Rain
Darkness
Light
easy.explanation: Although Egypt was dark, the Israelites had light in their dwellings.

medium.question: What happened after Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven?
answers: There was thick darkness throughout Egypt
The Israelites left Egypt
The Nile turned to blood
medium.explanation: After Moses stretched out his hand, thick darkness covered Egypt.

medium.question: In the phrase “darkness which may be felt,” what is emphasized?
answers: Bright light
Very heavy darkness
A strong wind
medium.explanation: The phrase describes darkness that was exceptionally deep and oppressive.

medium.question: Why did the Egyptians not rise from their places?
answers: They could not see even where they were
They were busy working
Moses forbade them to rise
medium.explanation: The darkness was so severe that the Egyptians could not see one another or move from their places.

challenge.question: What central contrast is emphasized in the passage?
answers: Egypt had darkness, while the Israelites had light
Egypt had light, while the Israelites had darkness
Egypt had rain, while Israel had drought
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts the darkness in Egypt with the light in the Israelites’ dwellings.

challenge.question: What can we conclude from the Egyptians’ darkness and the Israelites’ light?
answers: The darkness was only inside the houses
The plague distinguished between the Egyptians and the Israelites
The Israelites also could not see one another
challenge.explanation: The plague affected the Egyptians, while the Israelites continued to have light.

challenge.question: Which detail especially emphasizes the severity of the darkness?
answers: It appeared only in the sky
It lasted one hour
The Egyptians did not rise from their places for three days
challenge.explanation: The Egyptians’ inability to move for three days shows how deep and disabling the darkness was.

questions.question: What central contrast is emphasized in the passage?
answers: Egypt had darkness, while the Israelites had light
Egypt had light, while the Israelites had darkness
Egypt had rain, while Israel had drought
questions.explanation: The passage contrasts the darkness in Egypt with the light in the Israelites’ dwellings.

questions.question: What can we conclude from the Egyptians’ darkness and the Israelites’ light?
answers: The darkness was only inside the houses
The plague distinguished between the Egyptians and the Israelites
The Israelites also could not see one another
questions.explanation: The plague affected the Egyptians, while the Israelites continued to have light.

questions.question: Which detail especially emphasizes the severity of the darkness?
answers: It appeared only in the sky
It lasted one hour
The Egyptians did not rise from their places for three days
questions.explanation: The Egyptians’ inability to move for three days shows how deep and disabling the darkness was.

easy.question: Who called Moses and spoke to him?
answers: Pharaoh
Aaron
The Israelites
easy.explanation: The passage says that Pharaoh called Moses.

easy.question: According to Pharaoh, who could go with the Israelites?
answers: Only the elders
The children as well
Only the priests
easy.explanation: Pharaoh said that the children could go with them.

easy.question: What did Moses say they needed for worship?
answers: Clothing and tools
Bread and water
Sacrifices and burnt offerings
easy.explanation: Moses said they needed sacrifices and burnt offerings for the Lord.

medium.question: What was the disagreement between Pharaoh and Moses about the animals?
answers: Pharaoh wanted the animals left behind, while Moses insisted on taking them all
Pharaoh wanted to take all the animals, but Moses refused
They both agreed to leave the cattle in Egypt
medium.explanation: Pharaoh said the flocks and herds should stay, but Moses insisted that not a hoof be left behind.

medium.question: In the phrase “Our cattle also shall go with us,” what does “cattle” refer to?
answers: Their houses
Their animals
Their clothing
medium.explanation: The context makes clear that “cattle” refers to their livestock.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Moses takes the people, Pharaoh offers terms, and then they bring sacrifices
Moses asks to leave the children, Pharaoh agrees, and they return to Egypt
Pharaoh allows the children to go, Moses asks for sacrifices, and then insists on taking all the livestock
medium.explanation: First Pharaoh allows the children to go, then Moses asks for sacrifices, and finally he insists that all the livestock go too.

challenge.question: What does the statement “there shall not be an hoof be left behind” emphasize?
answers: Not even one animal should be left behind
Only cows would be taken
They did not need animals
challenge.explanation: The statement emphasizes that every animal would go with them.

challenge.question: Why did Moses say, “We know not with what we must serve the Lord, until we come thither”?
answers: They had forgotten how to worship the Lord
They did not yet know which animals would be required for worship
They did not intend to worship the Lord
challenge.explanation: Moses explained that they would know exactly what was needed for worship only after arriving.

challenge.question: What can we conclude from Moses’ response to Pharaoh’s offer?
answers: Moses accepted Pharaoh’s terms without change
Moses wanted to remain in Egypt with the animals
Moses would not accept partial permission and demanded complete freedom to worship
challenge.explanation: Moses rejected Pharaoh’s restriction and insisted that the families and all the livestock leave.

questions.question: What does the statement “there shall not be an hoof be left behind” emphasize?
answers: Not even one animal should be left behind
Only cows would be taken
They did not need animals
questions.explanation: The statement emphasizes that every animal would go with them.

questions.question: Why did Moses say, “We know not with what we must serve the Lord, until we come thither”?
answers: They had forgotten how to worship the Lord
They did not yet know which animals would be required for worship
They did not intend to worship the Lord
questions.explanation: Moses explained that they would know exactly what was needed for worship only after arriving.

questions.question: What can we conclude from Moses’ response to Pharaoh’s offer?
answers: Moses accepted Pharaoh’s terms without change
Moses wanted to remain in Egypt with the animals
Moses would not accept partial permission and demanded complete freedom to worship
questions.explanation: Moses rejected Pharaoh’s restriction and insisted that the families and all the livestock leave.

easy.question: What did Pharaoh do when the Lord hardened his heart?
answers: He refused to let the Israelites go
He sent Moses into the wilderness
He asked Moses for forgiveness
easy.explanation: The passage says that Pharaoh would not let the Israelites go.

easy.question: What did Pharaoh command Moses to do?
answers: Stay in the palace
Leave and never appear before him again
Bring the Israelites to him
easy.explanation: Pharaoh told Moses to leave and warned him not to see his face again.

easy.question: What did Moses answer Pharaoh?
answers: He would return the next day
He was afraid of dying
He would not see Pharaoh’s face again
easy.explanation: Moses replied that he would not see Pharaoh’s face again.

medium.question: What was the connection between the Lord hardening Pharaoh’s heart and Pharaoh’s decision?
answers: It caused Pharaoh to refuse to let the Israelites go
It caused Pharaoh to release Moses
It caused Pharaoh to ask Moses to return
medium.explanation: After the Lord hardened his heart, Pharaoh refused to let Israel go.

medium.question: In the phrase “he would not let them go,” what did Pharaoh’s refusal mean?
answers: He forgot about them
He did not want or agree to release them
He called out loudly
medium.explanation: In context, Pharaoh’s refusal means that he would not agree to release the Israelites.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Moses threatened Pharaoh, and Pharaoh released the people
Pharaoh saw Moses, and Moses asked to stay
Pharaoh ordered Moses to leave, threatened him, and Moses replied that he would not see him again
medium.explanation: Pharaoh first rejected Moses and threatened him; Moses then replied that he would not see Pharaoh again.

challenge.question: What can we conclude from Moses’ reply, “Thou hast spoken well”?
answers: Moses agreed that they would not meet again
Moses asked Pharaoh to change his mind
Moses apologized for his words
challenge.explanation: Moses acknowledged Pharaoh’s statement and confirmed that he would not see him again.

challenge.question: What notable grammatical contrast appears in the passage?
answers: Pharaoh speaks to the whole nation in the plural
Pharaoh addresses Moses in the singular, while the release refers to the Israelites in the plural
Moses addresses Pharaoh in the plural
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh speaks directly to Moses, but the statement about not letting “them” go refers to the Israelites.

challenge.question: According to verse 27, what is presented as the cause of Pharaoh’s refusal?
answers: His fear of Moses
His desire to keep the Israelites in the palace
The Lord’s hardening of his heart
challenge.explanation: The verse connects Pharaoh’s refusal with the Lord’s hardening of his heart.

questions.question: What can we conclude from Moses’ reply, “Thou hast spoken well”?
answers: Moses agreed that they would not meet again
Moses asked Pharaoh to change his mind
Moses apologized for his words
questions.explanation: Moses acknowledged Pharaoh’s statement and confirmed that he would not see him again.

questions.question: What notable grammatical contrast appears in the passage?
answers: Pharaoh speaks to the whole nation in the plural
Pharaoh addresses Moses in the singular, while the release refers to the Israelites in the plural
Moses addresses Pharaoh in the plural
questions.explanation: Pharaoh speaks directly to Moses, but the statement about not letting “them” go refers to the Israelites.

questions.question: According to verse 27, what is presented as the cause of Pharaoh’s refusal?
answers: His fear of Moses
His desire to keep the Israelites in the palace
The Lord’s hardening of his heart
questions.explanation: The verse connects Pharaoh’s refusal with the Lord’s hardening of his heart.
